title: The $9,000 Wedding Still Being Paid in 2032

scenes.say: 65 months of payments. That's what Aisha's $9,000 wedding on a card will take.
At roughly 24% a year, her card adds about $180 of interest in month one.
She pays $250 a month, so only about $70 touches the actual debt at first.
At that pace, the balance only hits zero in about five and a half years.
In total, she'd pay about $16,100. Around $7,100 is pure interest.
But at $450 a month, she's done in about 26 months, with roughly $2,600 interest.
That's about $4,500 kept, from the same card and the same wedding.
Would you pay $250, or push to $450? Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck.

question: Would you pay $250 a month, or push to $450 to be done in two years?
description: Aisha put about $9,000 of wedding costs on a card at roughly 24% APR. At $250 a month it takes about 65 months and around $16,100 in total; at $450 a month it's about 26 months and roughly $2,600 in interest. Estimates assume a fixed 24% APR and no new charges, rounded US numbers.
